title: Gideon and the Atlas
premise: In the river town of Marrow's Bend, on the eve of a revolution, Cyrus Eastwick — born to a typeface cutter and raised as neither son nor daughter, answering only to the name they carved for themselves — keeps the print shop's ledgers while the country slides toward war. When the army requisitions the town, the press, and the ledger bearing every family's name, Cyrus discovers their father has been forging documents for the rebellion, making the Eastwicks both indispensable and marked. As the ice thins on the river and evacuation berths dwindle to one, the army's captain — a man who once apprenticed beside Cyrus in the type room — offers a terrible bargain: the ledger's names in exchange for passage. Cyrus must choose between exposing the forged pages that could save hundreds, saving one sibling before the ice breaks, and admitting that invisibility was always an illusion. In the end, Cyrus burns the original ledger, gives the berth to their younger brother, stays behind to cut new type for a free press, and finds belonging not in escape but in the town that finally sees them.
about_author: Vesper Montrose is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in New England mill towns. Their fiction explores the quiet machinery of ordinary lives caught in historical gears.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Cyrus Eastwick introduces the print shop, measuring the world in ems and picas while cutting type beside their father, Aldous. A rumor of soldiers massing downriver arrives with the morning paper. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: tender routine shadowed by unease — the calm before requisition.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus records the town's debts and births in the great ledger, revealing how every family in Marrow's Bend is bound to the shop. Sibling tension flares when brother Tam demands his share of the business. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging defined by ink and obligation.

chapters.title: What the Captain Carried
chapters.summary: Captain Elias Vane arrives to requisition the press, and Cyrus recognizes him — the apprentice who left ten years ago without goodbye. Vane pretends not to know them. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: old wound reopened; love against duty takes its first shape.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers occupy the town square; the army claims the ledger as evidence of sedition. Aldous burns nothing but grows strangely calm. Cyrus notices fresh type hidden beneath the floorboards. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tam's Ambition
chapters.summary: Tam courts the occupying officers, believing collaboration will buy the family safety. Cyrus watches their brother trade jokes for favors and feels the family fracturing. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into self-deception.

chapters.title: The Forged Pages
chapters.summary: Cyrus discovers Aldous has been printing false travel passes for rebels — the very crime the army hunts. Father and daughter-son confront each other over the case of hidden sorts. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with fierce pride.

chapters.title: Ice Sounds at Night
chapters.summary: The river groans; spring thaw approaches, and with it the last ferry north. Sister Wren counts the family's savings against the price of one berth. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet arithmetic of survival, love measured in coin.

chapters.title: An Old Apprenticeship
chapters.summary: Vane returns alone after hours, asking Cyrus to set a notice condemning the rebellion. Over the composing stone, ten years of silence break. POV: alternating memory, Cyrus present. Emotional beat: intimacy rekindled inside complicity.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Vane reveals the army suspects a printer among the rebels and offers Cyrus immunity for a name. Cyrus lies fluently for the first time. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren secretly negotiates with a smuggler for two berths, planning to leave without telling Aldous. Cyrus catches her counting coins at midnight. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sisterly love expressed as escape plans.

chapters.title: Aldous Teaches Cutting
chapters.summary: Knowing he may hang, Aldous teaches Cyrus to cut a full alphabet from steel — the inheritance no army can seize. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: elegiac transmission; power passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers tear apart the shop hunting rebel broadsides. Cyrus hides the forged passes inside a forme locked for tomorrow's official gazette. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: breathless suspense; wit as resistance.

chapters.title: Tam's Ledger Entry
chapters.summary: Tam, drunk on officer company, hints that the Eastwicks' ledger holds irregularities. Cyrus realizes their brother may sell them all. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: corruption completing its arc; pity replacing anger.

chapters.title: Night Composing
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Vane print a secret edition of rebel news together, hands nearly touching over the tympan. Both know it is treason. POV: dual. Emotional beat: love consummated in shared risk.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks Early
chapters.summary: A warm wind cracks the river ahead of schedule; the smuggler's boat leaves at dawn instead of next week. The family has hours, not days. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: panic compressing every choice.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: The smuggler honors only one passage. The family gathers to decide who goes — Aldous insists on Tam, Wren refuses to abandon Cyrus, Tam assumes it is his by right. POV: rotating voices. Emotional beat: the blurb's central choice made flesh.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Chose
chapters.summary: Cyrus puts Tam on the boat at gunpoint of their own conscience, staying behind with Wren and Aldous. Tam departs weeping, unrepentant. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief and strange peace; duty inverted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Before the army can seize it, Cyrus feeds the original ledger to the press's fire, destroying the names the army needs — and the proof that could condemn the town. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; erasure as salvation.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to arrest the Eastwicks, Vane reports the ledger destroyed and the forger fled, falsifying his first report. He meets Cyrus at the riverbank and says goodbye properly this time. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: love choosing duty's opposite; bittersweet parting.

chapters.title: After the Requisition
chapters.summary: The army withdraws as the revolution reaches the capital. The town, nameless now in any official record, begins rebuilding from memory. Aldous coughs blood but smiles. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exhausted dawn; community reforged.

chapters.title: New Type
chapters.summary: Cyrus cuts a fresh alphabet — including letters for their own chosen name — and prints the first free edition of the town paper on the scarred old press. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: identity claimed; craft as rebirth.

chapters.title: The Atlas Open
chapters.summary: Years later, Tam's letters arrive from the north; Wren runs the shop; Vane's postmark appears without words. Cyrus opens the atlas on the counter and marks Marrow's Bend — no longer invisible, exactly where they chose to stand. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the world measured in what was carried, and what stayed.
